observations: A medical module labeled 'BIS Engine' for use with Philips patient monitors.
A smaller grey component labeled 'BIS XP' and 'DSC-XP' (Digital Signal Converter) is connected.
Several grey interface cables are coiled on a wooden desk.

The background shows an iMac computer and a power strip.
There is a watermark '3SETMED LTD' and 'POSTED ON Jiji' across the center.

claims.claim: BIS (Bispectral Index) engine with Philips refers to using Philips' patient monitoring systems
claims.evidence: Photo 0 shows the module label explicitly stating 'BIS Engine' and 'For use with Philips'.

risks.risk: The module may be non-functional or unable to communicate with a host monitor.
risks.proof: A video showing the module connected to a Philips monitor, powering on, and successfully processing a signal.

risks.risk: The internal wiring of the cables or the pins in the connectors may be damaged.
risks.proof: Close-up photos of all connector pins and a video showing no 'cable fault' errors when the system is moved.

risks.risk: The specific model number (e.g., M1034A vs M1034B) which determines compatibility and value is not legible.
risks.proof: A clear, high-resolution photo of the manufacturer's label on the side or back of the module showing the REF/Model number.
risks.if_unproven: as the oldest/least valuable compatible model

proof_requests: Clear photo of the identification label on the side of the BIS Engine module showing the REF and SN numbers.
Video of the unit connected to a Philips monitor showing it is recognized by the system.
Close-up photos of the connector ends for both the module and the DSC-XP unit.
response.reason: The item is clearly identified by brand and type from the photos. While the exact sub-model number is not legible, it can be priced at its worst-case (untested/oldest version) value.
